patch_description: The current exponential-weighted moving average induces significant lag (0.38 lag error) and many spurious slope changes (223) because it's a causal smoother whose effective center of mass sits well behind the newest sample. A far better approach for the four objectives: fit a local quadratic (or linear, rank-deficient-safe) polynomial to each window via least squares and evaluate it at the *most recent* window sample. This is a Savitzky-Golay-style endpoint estimator: (1) it has near-zero phase/lag because the fit extrapolates to the window's leading edge rather than averaging behind it; (2) the quadratic term captures local curvature so genuine trends and turning points are preserved (tracking accuracy); (3) polynomial least squares acts as a low-pass projection that strongly suppresses uncorrelated noise (noise reduction, smoothness); (4) the estimated local slope from the fitted derivative is far more stable than finite differences of a noisy average, drastically reducing false reversals and slope changes. To make it robust, I: (a) fit the quadratic with scaled time coordinates for numerical conditioning, (b) detect when a window is in a fast-varying regime and shrink the effective window (adaptive windowing) to avoid over-smoothing genuine dynamics, and (c) fall back to a linear fit when the quadratic system is ill-conditioned. I keep the same output length and function signatures so the rest of the program (alignment via `delay`, metrics) still works unchanged.
